\caption{Compression, trained on 5\,GB of FineWeb per language (the \texttt{quick} read-until-full sample, which is not uniform over the source), 34{,}685 matched total vocabulary, evaluated on held-out Goldfish. \plainscheme{} is the mean absolute baseline in characters per token, every other compression cell the mean percentage change against it, positive meaning better compression. \bnds{w} $<$ \bnds{wp} $<$ \bnds{wpd} throughout. MA is MorphAlign (IBM1 alignment at threshold 0.01, scaled by 100) and MS is MorphScore $F_1$ with an unsplit word credited rather than dropped, both on English and both higher-is-better. Where a scheme's two probes disagree the cell reads bare/in-context and only the in-context score is ranked: segmenting a gold word on its own is unreachable for a leading-space vocabulary, so \plainscheme{} is scored there on splits it does not make in running text. \textbf{Bold} is the best and \underline{underline} the runner-up within a column, ties sharing a place. Per-language numbers in Table~\ref{tab:intrinsic-quick}. Each compression mean covers the languages that have that scheme.}
